When will I use this?

Area and perimeter: when will I use this?

Whenever you cover, paint, plant or mark out a space.

Painter and decorator

Route: Construction and the built environment

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

A room is 4 m by 3.5 m, with walls 2.5 m high. There is a 2 m² door and a 3.5 m² window. Two coats; the tin says 1 litre covers 16 m² (example figure).

  1. Perimeter: \(4 + 3.5 + 4 + 3.5 = 15\) m.
  2. Wall area: \(15 \times 2.5 = 37.5\) m².
  3. Take away door and window: \(37.5 - 5.5 = 32\) m².
  4. Two coats: 64 m². Paint: \(64 \div 16 = 4\) litres.

Groundsperson (sports turf)

Route: Agriculture, environmental and animal care

Groundspeople mark out pitches. The FA's recommended adult pitch is 100 m long and 64 m wide.

  1. Lines round the edge (perimeter): \(2 \times (100 + 64) = 328\) m of white line.
  2. Grass to cut (area): \(100 \times 64 = 6400\) m².

Farmer

Route: Agriculture, environmental and animal care

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Fertiliser is spread at a rate in kg per hectare. 1 hectare = 10 000 m². A field is 250 m by 120 m; the plan is 150 kg per hectare (example figure).

  1. Area: \(250 \times 120 = 30\,000\) m² = 3 ha.
  2. Fertiliser: \(3 \times 150 = 450\) kg.

Practise it

Games on MaffsGames that practise area and perimeter:

  • Formula Plug-In: Substitute values into formulae and work out the answer, from simple rules to area and speed.
  • New Shapes: Area of parallelograms and trapezia, and volume of prisms.
  • Take a Walk: Perimeter and area on sports pitches: walk round the edge, or cover the grass. Rectangles, compound shapes and circles.

For parents and carers: our guide to Area & Perimeter.

Sources

Every job and every figure that is not an example comes from a public page you can check.

  • Painter and decorator: Dulux, "How much paint do you need?"
  • Groundsperson (sports turf): The FA, "Guide to pitch and goalpost dimensions"; Skills England, Sports turf operative standard (ST0210), which lists marking out playing surfaces
  • Farmer: AHDB, Nutrient Management Guide (RB209), which gives every rate in kg/ha
